description: Upload multiple ObjectScript files from a local directory into IRIS. Accepts a glob pattern to match files. File paths are mapped to IRIS document names (path separators become dots). Optionally compiles all uploaded documents afterward. This is the preferred way to deploy ObjectScript classes to IRIS — always create or edit .cls files on disk first, then use this tool to upload and compile. This ensures all code is source-controlled and reviewable. Uploads whose path-derived document name disagrees with the file's own Class/ROUTINE declaration are refused with both names named — this guards against trap-shaped globs (wildcard AFTER the package directory, e.g. 'src/MyPkg/*.cls') silently stripping the package prefix. A leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped before upload, and a per-document error reported by the server in the PUT response (e.g. an illegal header line) is surfaced as an upload failure rather than counted as a success. For an existing class, a file whose content drops one of the class's Storage definitions is refused and nothing is stored for that file (a failures entry with code STORAGE_DROPPED; the other files continue), because IRIS would generate new storage at the next compile, which can change how existing rows are read; allowStorageRegeneration (default false) lets it through, and the result names the dropped definitions.

allowStorageRegeneration.description: Boolean (true/false), default false. When false, a class file whose content drops one of the Storage definitions the class has now is refused (a failures entry with code STORAGE_DROPPED; nothing is stored for that file, and the other files continue); changing a Storage definition's content is allowed. When true, the file is uploaded, IRIS generates new storage at the next compile (which can change how existing rows are read), and the result's storageDrops names the dropped definitions. No effect on a new class or on other document types.

baseDir.description: Optional. Directory used verbatim as the base for document name mapping, INSTEAD of inferring the base from the glob pattern's first wildcard segment (e.g. baseDir='c:/projects/src' with path='c:/projects/src/MyPkg/*.cls' maps MyPkg/ClassA.cls to 'MyPkg.ClassA.cls'). Use it to state the package root deterministically when the glob's wildcard cannot precede the package directory.

compile.description: When true, compile all successfully uploaded documents after upload (default: false)

flags.description: Compilation flags (e.g., 'ck', 'cku'). Only used when compile is true

ignoreConflict.description: If true (default), each file overwrites its server copy without a version check. If false, a file whose document already exists is saved under a version check: it is overwritten unless the document changes on the server while it is being saved, in which case that file fails with DOCUMENT_CONFLICT and the others continue.

path.description: Glob pattern for files to upload (e.g., 'c:/projects/src/**/*.cls'). The directory prefix before the first glob metacharacter is used as the base for document name mapping — so the wildcard must come BEFORE the package directory: 'c:/projects/src/**/*.cls' maps MyPkg/ClassA.cls to 'MyPkg.ClassA.cls', but 'c:/projects/src/MyPkg/*.cls' swallows MyPkg into the base and would map to the unqualified 'ClassA.cls'. Mismatched uploads are refused when the file's own Class/ROUTINE declaration disagrees; pass baseDir to state the package root deterministically.

server.description: Named server profile to target for this call (from `IRIS_PROFILES`). Omit to use the default server.

name: iris_doc_load
title: Bulk Load Documents
